# Marcelo B. Diani — Senior Full Stack Developer & Team Lead

> Senior Full Stack Developer with 7+ years of experience specializing in TypeScript, React, and Node.js. Computer Engineer graduated from the University of São Paulo (USP) and mathematics olympiad gold medalist. Led teams of up to 6 developers managing 14 Shopify apps serving tens of thousands of daily users. Worked in EdTech, FinTech and E-commerce companies. Top 4% Cursor AI user worldwide in 2025. Positive mindset, driven by improving people's lives through technology.

## About Marcelo

Marcelo B. Diani is a Senior Full Stack Developer and Team Lead with over 7 years of professional experience building production-grade web applications. He graduated in Computer Engineering from the University of São Paulo (USP) in São Carlos, Brazil, in 2019, finishing in the top 10 of 61 students with no failed courses.

Born in 1996 in Mirassol, a small city in the countryside of São Paulo, Brazil, Marcelo grew up in a humble and hardworking family. His father fixes TVs, radios, and electronics — watching him sparked Marcelo's curiosity about how things work. He won a gold medal at the OBMEP national mathematics olympiad and participated in a 4-year program at UNESP for medalists.

His mission is to improve people's lives through technology. He is always open to new opportunities and interesting conversations.

### Clearer.io — Senior Full Stack Developer / Team Lead / Scrum Master (2022–2025)
Location: Boston, Massachusetts (Remote)

- Led two teams (3 and 6 developers) as Team Lead and Scrum Master, owning PR reviews, sprint planning and meetings, 1:1s, interviews and delivery tracking with Jellyfish, improving on-time delivery rate across the team.
- Managed 14 Shopify App Store products (bundles, upsells, checkout, returns, currency conversion) serving tens of thousands of daily users and generating multi-million dollar annual revenue.
- Migrated all managed applications from Heroku to AWS using a reusable Infrastructure as Code (IaC) library built with Cloud Development Kit (CDK), reducing hosting costs.
- Increased test coverage from zero by introducing unit and end-to-end tests via Datadog Synthetic Monitoring, reducing production regressions. Added Codacy for static analysis.
- Reduced average debugging time by implementing observability (logging and distributed tracing) in Datadog. Built a Memcached caching layer that eliminated database timeouts on heavy product queries, and a Lambda function using DynamoDB and LLMs to auto-generate customized storefront widgets.
- Developed tools that boosted merchant revenue and enhanced user experience across the entire e-commerce conversion funnel. Resolved live critical production integration issues across diverse e-commerce storefronts.
- Tech stack: JavaScript, TypeScript, Node.js, React, Next.js, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, REST, Redis, React Native, AWS, CDK, DataDog, Heroku, Codacy, Jellyfish, Cloudflare, Shopify.

### Acesso Comercial — Founder (2021–2022)
Location: São Carlos, São Paulo

- Founded and built an e-commerce platform (Shopify alternative) for small businesses, featuring ERP, CRM, SSR blog, and omnichannel chat with websockets, onboarding over 600 stores.
- Architected 5 microservices (auth, core, metrics, payments, messaging) with Blue-Green deployment via GitHub Actions, Docker, and Nginx. Monitored with Prometheus, Tempo, OpenTelemetry, Loki, and Grafana. Used BullMQ with Redis for async workers.
- Built the platform with React, Node.js, GraphQL, Relay, and MongoDB; integrated 10+ third-party APIs (shipping, payments, Google Console, Facebook Business). Implemented AI features using OpenAI, Gemini, and RAG with Typesense as vector store.
- Led a team of 2 developers and 1 support specialist, coordinating with designers, media buyers, lawyers, and external consultants.
- Achieved 1,000+ automated tests (unit, integration, and end-to-end) with Mocha, Sinon, Chai, and Cypress, maintaining high code coverage.
- Collaborated directly with more than 30 merchants via on-site and remote sessions to co-design product features and provide ongoing technical support.
- Allocated over $10K in ad spend across paid media channels, driving platform growth and user engagement through data-driven campaigns.
- Tech stack: TypeScript, Node.js, React, Next.js, MongoDB, GraphQL, AWS, GitHub Actions, Docker, WebSocket, LLMs, RAG, SSR, BullMQ, Redis.

### Vórtx DTVM — Full Stack Developer (2020–2021)
Location: São Paulo, São Paulo

- Upgraded and launched a legacy Angular/.NET platform into production.
- Built and maintained a client data management platform for investment fund operations using Angular, .NET Core, 3 microservices, and 2 Lambda functions connected to a MongoDB cluster and SQL Server.
- Migrated 1,800 manually stored Excel records to an automated online platform, eliminating manual effort.
- Delivered the platform to external users in 6 months, on schedule and within budget.
- Implemented refresh token authentication, reducing daily login friction for all users to a single sign-in per day.
- Introduced backend pagination and restructured the database schema, reducing query response time from multiple seconds to under 500ms.
- Generated 200,000 dynamic PDFs with Puppeteer for client-facing financial reports, delivering ahead of schedule to ensure Federal compliance and avoid regulatory fines.
- Tech stack: C#, .NET, JavaScript, Angular, SQL Server, MongoDB, REST, GitHub Actions, Lambda, Puppeteer, Microservices, Clean Architecture.

Location: São Carlos, São Paulo

- Developed 2 platforms from scratch (postgraduate courses and a revamp of an old platform) serving 13,000+ active law students, built with React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, and GraphQL.
- Redesigned the front-end architecture using Atomic Design, breaking a monolithic codebase into reusable components and reducing maintenance effort.
- Built a real-time student analytics dashboard connected to a Kafka event system, giving users visibility into their course progress and engagement.
- Created a configurable database seeder that eliminated the need for production data in local development, speeding up developer onboarding and testing.
